items.evidence: The financial component of our STIP program is based on two financial metrics: Sales (50%) and Incentive Operating Income (50%).
The remaining 33% of their STIP is based on a team scorecard, designed to strongly align pay to Target's strategic agenda.
market share gains in Apparel & Accessories, Home, Essentials & Beauty, Food & Beverage, and at the enterprise level
digital channel sales that continue to outpace the industry
numerous new store openings and remodels
The three relative metrics used in our PSU plan are:
The payout is further subject to an incremental additive or subtractive modification based on sales growth compared to Target's Census addressable market growth
Adjusted Sales growth. The compound annual growth rate in Adjusted Sales over the performance period, relative to our retail peer group.
EPS growth. The compound annual growth rate of our EPS versus the reported EPS of our retail peer group.
ROIC. Three-year average net operating profit after-tax divided by average invested capital
The market share and EPS growth metrics utilize a base year of fiscal 2016 and a final performance year of fiscal 2019
The PBRSU amount will be adjusted up or down by 25 percentage points if Target's TSR is in the top one-third or bottom one-third
